translation.english_title: Let us lay out a new path

english_lines: Let us lay out a new path — we — the evil,
Path that leads to fighting, we shall bring it down...
By labouring every day, we shall rise —
Without straying from the path, we shall live —
notes: The broken source syntax around `நாம் - கெட்ட / போரிடும் பாதையை` is not silently rewritten into a cleaner Tamil sentence; the English keeps the interruption while making the target of `சாய்ப்போம்` explicit enough to read.
`உழைத்தே உயர்வோம்` retains the labour/rise pairing central to the song's social programme.

english_lines: The barren waste of ignorance — with the plough-point,
That is good knowledge...
The barren waste of ignorance — with the plough-point,
That is good knowledge...
With the plough-point that is knowledge...
notes: The agricultural metaphor is kept concrete: ignorance is barren land and knowledge is the plough-point.
The full repetition is preserved instead of being reduced to one occurrence.

english_lines: With the great knowledge of science — ploughing,
We are those who seek true wisdom!
With the great knowledge of science — ploughing,
We are those who seek true wisdom!
notes: `விஞ்ஞானம் / மெய்ஞ்ஞானம்` is retained as science / true wisdom, while `உழுதே` continues the ploughing metaphor rather than becoming an abstract intellectual verb.

english_lines: We shall live rising upward — with the times,
We shall change along with change,
We shall change along with change.
notes: The repeated `மாற்றம் / மாறுவோம்` change-language is kept visibly repetitive instead of varied for English style.

english_lines: With knowledge springing forth — with new,
Tools we shall take command — we,
With knowledge springing forth — with new,
Tools we shall take command — we!
notes: The springing-water image in `ஊற்றெடுக்கும் அறிவு` and the material `புதிய கருவி` remain visible; the stanza is not generalized into modernization rhetoric.

english_lines: We'll plant the seedlings — the weeds,
We'll yank up and throw away!
We'll plant the seedlings — the weeds,
We'll yank up and throw away!
We'll guard and grow them — the grain-head,
Seeing it, we'll rejoice — the grain-head,
Seeing it, we'll rejoice...
notes: The colloquial agricultural vocabulary `நாத்து` and `பேத்து` is translated by its field-work action rather than replaced with formal agronomy language.
The seedlings/weeds/grain-head sequence preserves the song's labouring physicality.

english_lines: By the grace of the god who came in a dream,
They say Nandanar raised the crop...
As always, with the help of our hands and legs,
We raised the crop this day...
notes: The Nandanar miracle reference is kept beside the deliberately material counter-image of hands and legs doing the work; the contrast is not softened or explained away.

source_tamil_lines: வாழ்வில் இன்பம் பொங்கிட வந்தாய் எங்கள் தோழியே...
english_lines: In the bending ear of grain you ripened and came, O golden queen...
You came, our comrade, so joy may overflow in life...
“We have found a common granary,
We have laid out a new path” ...
notes: The ripened grain becomes `தங்கராணி` — golden queen — and then `தோழி` — comrade; both shifts are retained.
`பொதுக் களஞ்சியம்` remains `common granary`, preserving the collective-economic image rather than translating it as mere prosperity.

translator_notes: This translation keeps the song's distinctive chain: ignorance as wasteland, knowledge as plough-point, science as the force that ploughs, new tools, collective field labour, Nandanar's miracle contrasted with hands-and-legs labour, and the common granary.
Political and rationalist force is retained without importing modern terminology not present in the source.
Because song 009 spans PDF 38–39, the record preserves both source pages as one song provenance.
This is a literary source-faithful translation, not a singable adaptation.
